newsitem.title: USA: Eastwood trial heads to closing arguments Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Eastwood trial heads to closing arguments Thursday.

text.p: Testimony in Sondra Locke's civil suit against ex-lover Clint Eastwood wrapped up on Wednesday with the judge scheduling closing arguments for Thursday.
Locke, who met Eastwood on the set of their 1975 movie "The Outlaw Josey Wales", alleges in her suit that Eastwood undermined her contract with Warner Bros Pictures to direct films for the studio.
The 49-year-old actress took the stand briefly on Wednesday to testify about her relationship with Eastwood and answer questions about her contract with the studio.
Locke, who lived with Eastwood for 13 years, originally filed a "palimony" suit in 1989, claiming assets the couple accumulated during their relationship.
She later dropped the suit when Eastwood agreed to secure her a director's contract worth $1.5 million at Warner Bros.

Locke says her Warner Bros contract was "a sham" because Eastwood had a secret deal with the studio to reimburse it for losses incurred by any film she directed. She is seeking damages of more than $2.5 million.
Judge David Schacter scheduled closing arguments for Thursday. The six man, six woman jury is expected to begin deliberations on Thursday afternoon.
